privacy.trigger: No uploads · No storage · No tracking
privacy.title: How these promises are kept
privacy.description: You can check every one of them yourself; no need to take our word for it.
privacy.noUploadBody: What you enter is processed in this page only and never sent anywhere. The Content Security Policy sets connect-src none, which the browser enforces, so the page couldn't send anything even if it tried. Link Transfer puts its content after the # in the address, which is never sent to the server when the link is opened. The offline cache downloads and periodically checks this site's own files; those requests carry nothing you entered.
privacy.noStorageBody: No cookies, localStorage or IndexedDB; not even the theme or language preference is saved. A language you pick is kept only in the address. The offline cache holds nothing but this site's code, styles, fonts and icons. Close the tab and everything you entered is gone.
privacy.noTrackingBody: No analytics, no third-party scripts, no CDN. All code ships with the site, and the source is public.
privacy.verify: To check: open the Network panel in your browser's developer tools and use any tool; no new requests will appear. After one visit, the site keeps working offline.

pwa.updateWithSecrets: It takes effect after a reload, which clears the 2FA secrets you've added. You can reload when you're done.
pwa.updatePlain: It takes effect after a reload, which clears what you've entered on the page.

share.description: Encode content into a link and open it on another device to read it.

help.plain1: For content that isn't sensitive, such as sending a URL to your own phone.
help.plain2: Anyone with the link can read it; just open the link or scan the code.
help.key1: The sender provides the key: a random one is made for each encryption.
help.key2: Send the encrypted content and the key to the receiver separately.
help.key3: To send several items, turn on Fixed key so the receiver enters it only once.
help.public1: The receiver provides the key: they create a public key on the receive page and give it to the sender.
help.public2: The sender encrypts with that public key and sends the result; no key needs to be passed along.

share.contentPlaceholder: Paste text to send to another device, such as a subscription link, a config snippet or a quick note
share.plainDescription: The content goes into the link as plain text.
share.publicDescription: X25519 key agreement with AES-256-GCM. Only the receive page that created the public key can decrypt it.
share.scanPublicKey: Scan a public key QR code
share.scanPublicKeyDescription: Point the camera at the public key QR code on the receiver's page.
share.notPublicKey: This isn't a public key QR code
share.recipientInvalid: This isn't a valid public key. Paste the full key from the receive page.
share.recipientHint: The receiver creates it under Decrypt › Public key on the receive page.
share.fixedKeyDescription: Reuse one key across generations, so the receiver enters it only once.
share.tooLong: Too much content: the link would exceed {{limit}} characters, more than browsers and chat apps can reliably carry. Shorten the content or send it as a file.
share.localhost: You're on localhost, so the link won't open on other devices. Use a LAN address (such as the one shown by pnpm dev:lan) or the live site instead.
share.history: Opened links stay in the browser history; encrypt anything sensitive.
share.plainResult: Not encrypted: anyone with the link can read the content.
share.longLink: This link is long, and some chat apps or mail clients may cut it short. If the receiver is told the content is incomplete, send it as a file instead.
share.linkNoQr: Too much content for a QR code. Copy the link and send it instead.
share.reserveShort: The QR code works now, but the same content may no longer fit if the site moves to a longer address.
share.contentNoQr: Too much content for a QR code. Copy it and send it instead.
share.contentHint: No address included. Read it with Scan on the receive page; you can scan several in a row.
share.publicKeyNote: No key to pass along: open the encrypted content or link on the receive page that created the public key.
share.keyNote: It can't be recovered after you leave this page. Send it separately from the link.

receive.waiting: The content is encrypted. Enter the key the sender gave you.
receive.keyMismatch: Wrong key: it can't decrypt this content
receive.scanKeyDescription: Point the camera at the key QR code on the sender's page.
receive.publicIntro: Let the sender encrypt with your public key. The private key never leaves this page, so no key needs to be passed along.
receive.publicShare: Give the public key to the sender, or let them scan the QR code to open the send page directly. Receive the content on this page by pasting or scanning.
receive.privateKeyNote: The private key exists only in this page's memory. Back it up before reloading or closing the page.
receive.privateKeyBackup: Back up the private key before reloading or closing this page; restore it later with Import private key.
receive.privateKeyWarning: The private key can decrypt everything sent to this public key. Keep it only as your own backup and never give it to anyone.
receive.importDescription: Paste a private key you backed up to restore its public key and the ability to decrypt.
receive.privateKeyInvalid: This isn't a valid private key
receive.replaceWarning: This replaces the current public and private keys.
receive.scanContentDescription: Point the camera at content QR codes; you can scan several in a row.
receive.pastePlaceholder: Or paste a link or content
receive.volatile: Nothing here, content or keys, survives reloading or closing the page.
receive.publicNoPage: This content is encrypted to a public key, and only the page that created that key can decrypt it. Paste the link or scan it on that page.
receive.publicWrongPage: This content wasn't encrypted to this page's public key.
receive.receivedWaiting: Received; set the key to decrypt it
receive.keyChanged: The current key can't decrypt the new content. The sender may have changed keys.
receive.keyCannotOpen: The current key can't decrypt this content

otp.description: Generate codes from 2FA secrets. Secrets stay only in this tab's memory and are cleared on reload.
otp.secretPlaceholder: Paste a secret or otpauth:// link
otp.pasteHint: Pasting several lines splits them into rows.
otp.advancedHint: Change these only if the service asks you to.
otp.dropHint: You can also paste or drop a QR code screenshot.
otp.noQrFound: No QR code found. Take a clearer or more complete screenshot of the code.
otp.duplicates_one: {{count}} entry is already in the list and was skipped
otp.duplicates_other: {{count}} entries are already in the list and were skipped
otp.tempUse: Meant for occasional or emergency use. Typing the password and generating the code on the same computer defeats the "second factor" of 2FA; use an authenticator app on your phone for important accounts.
otp.empty: Codes appear here once you add secrets. Click a code to copy it.
otp.utcNote: Codes are based on UTC. If they keep failing, make sure the system clock and time zone are set automatically.
otp.codeCopyFailed: Couldn't copy. Type the code manually.
otp.exportDescription: Scan it with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or a similar app on your phone.
otp.exportWarning: This QR code contains the secret itself: anyone who scans it can generate your codes. Close it when you're done and don't keep a screenshot.
